sources.entry: Saga Reader - AI-powered web and RSS reader. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/dyerc/Doughnut)

summary.one_liner: Saga Reader is a free, open-source, cross-platform desktop app (Rust, Tauri, Svelte) that pulls web and RSS content on user-chosen keywords and uses cloud or local LLMs to summarize and discuss it.
summary.what_it_does: The app retrieves internet content based on user-defined keywords and interests, using search and RSS retrieval modes. A Rust-based scraping module fetches results from search engines, and an article optimization workflow processes them with LLMs. Articles can be summarized, auto-translated into the user's preferred language, and discussed with an AI reading companion during reading. Users can read in a built-in viewer or open articles in their browser. Articles, interests and data are stored locally on the user's computer, and background updates and article search are supported. The README says it runs on Windows, Mac, and Linux.
use_cases: Chatting with an AI about what you are reading
Private local storage of reading history
how_to_run: bun install (or pnpm install / npm install)
bun run build (builds for the host system; build:macos or build:windows scripts for cross-compiling)
notable: AI-driven interactive reading companion for discussing articles
Supports both cloud LLM providers and local models via Ollama
Keyword-based subscriptions without manual feed setup
Claims memory use under 10MB and runs on older computers
Local-first storage; no ads or tracking per README
caveats: The README points to an external Help Document for installation precautions and LLM configuration, which was not included
Development requires Rust and Bun (or Node.js) toolchains
Cross-platform builds are described as host-only by default; cross-compiling needs the separate macOS or Windows scripts
